one_line: Afghan emperor Sher Shah Suri and a village patwari, shaping early Mughal-era land revenue records on the Gangetic plain.

appearance.age_look: Sher Shah: late 40s, broad-shouldered and sturdy; Patwari: early 30s, lean and slightly bookish.
appearance.face: Sher Shah has a square face, wheatish-brown complexion, strong jaw, thick brows, short trimmed beard and calm, assessing eyes with a firm but fair default expression; the Patwari has an oval face, lighter wheatish complexion, neatly trimmed moustache, thin brows and focused, slightly earnest eyes.
appearance.hair: Sher Shah’s hair is black with subtle grey at the temples, kept short under a padded, dome-shaped Afghan-style turban in deep rust-red with a narrow gold border; the Patwari has straight dark-brown hair, tied in a small knot at the back, mostly hidden under a simple off-white cotton turban wrapped low and snug.
appearance.costume: Sher Shah wears a long, full-sleeved Afghan-style jama reaching mid-calf in deep bottle-green wool with a subtle woven herringbone texture, crossed and tied at the side with a wide russet-brown leather belt that has a simple brass buckle; over this he has a sleeveless, hip-length quilted waistcoat in warm ochre with faint vertical stitching, and loose cream-colored cotton churidar trousers gathered at the ankles, with sturdy brown leather riding boots; the Patwari wears a knee-length, straight-cut off-white cotton kurta with narrow cuffs and a slightly longer hem at the back, paired with light khaki cotton dhoti neatly pleated and tied at the waist, the ends brought forward and back in tidy folds, and simple dark-brown leather sandals; the Patwari also has a narrow indigo cotton angavastra shawl draped over one shoulder, with thin white stripes along the edges, and a small cloth pouch at his waist for ink and seals.
appearance.signature: Sher Shah carries a slightly curved Indo-Afghan steel sword with a plain disc hilt at his left hip in a dark-brown leather scabbard, while the Patwari holds a rolled palm-leaf or paper land record scroll tied with a red cotton cord and a wooden ink pen tucked behind his ear.

ref_desc: Sher Shah Suri has a square wheatish-brown face, short black hair with grey at the temples under a rust-red Afghan turban, a deep bottle-green jama with ochre waistcoat, cream churidar and brown boots, carrying a curved sword, beside a lean patwari in off-white kurta, khaki dhoti, simple turban and indigo shawl holding a red-tied land record scroll.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two characters standing side by side: Sher Shah Suri is a sturdy, late-40s Afghan emperor with a square wheatish-brown face, strong jaw, short black hair greying at the temples under a deep rust-red dome-shaped Afghan turban with a narrow gold border, thick brows and a short trimmed beard, wearing a long deep bottle-green wool jama crossing at the chest and tied at the side with a wide russet-brown leather belt, over which sits a sleeveless hip-length quilted ochre waistcoat with subtle vertical stitching, paired with loose cream-colored cotton churidar trousers and sturdy brown leather riding boots, a slightly curved Indo-Afghan steel sword with a plain disc hilt hanging at his left hip in a dark-brown leather scabbard, his default expression calm and assessing; beside him stands a village patwari in his early 30s, lean and slightly bookish, with an oval face, lighter wheatish complexion, neatly trimmed moustache, thin brows and focused eyes, straight dark-brown hair tied in a small knot under a simple off-white cotton turban wrapped low and snug, wearing a knee-length off-white cotton kurta with narrow cuffs over a neatly pleated light khaki cotton dhoti tied at the waist, the folds clearly visible, simple dark-brown leather sandals, a narrow indigo cotton angavastra shawl with thin white edge stripes draped over one shoulder, a small pouch at his waist, a wooden ink pen tucked behind his ear and a rolled palm-leaf or paper land record scroll tied with a red cotton cord in his hand; show them head-to-toe with clear front view, consistent colors, and clean, historically grounded Gangetic-plain Mughal-era styling emphasizing Sher Shah’s authority and the patwari’s record-keeping role.
